newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Dec 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The country's top businessmen, members of the powerful Makati Business Club and the Management Association of the Philippines, oppose moves to amend the Constition and extend the term of President Fidel Ramos (MANILA TIMES/INQUIRER)
- The Philippines Energy Regulatory Board will announce today another round of price adjustments with a slight reduction in the prices of fuel oil and gasoline (ALL NEWSPAPERS)

- Senate President Ernesto Maceda dares a Thai national involved in the allegedly anomalous sale of a reclaimed property to Amari Development Corp to return to the Philippines and face a Senate inquiry (MALAYA)
- President Ramos appeals to organisers of a group seeking to amend the Constitution and extend the term of the President to drop their bid. (STANDARD)

- Protestant pastors say they favor constitutional amendments allowing President Ramos to seek re-election, going agaoinst the strong opposition of the Philippines' Roman Catholic Church to changes in the constitution. (PHILIPPINE STAR)

- Tokai Bank of Japan obtains approval from the Central Bank's Monetary Board to buy 30 percent of Global Business Bank, a commercial bank where Metropolitan Bank and Trust Co has a 49 percent stake (ALL NEWSPAPERS).
- The World Bank says the Philippines will continue to rely on the private sector for the bulk of the projected $9 billion in external financing over the next two years (INQUIRER)
- Far East Bank and Trust Co is in the lookout for partners following a trend toward bank mergers (MALAYA)

- The country's top businessmen, members of the Makati Business Club and the Management Association of the Philippines, express confidence the economy will grow by 7 to 7.5 percent next year and that inflation could be contained at 6.5 to seven percent (BULLETIN/TODAY)

- The World Bank urges the Philippine government to scrap all fiscal and monetary policies which provide preferential treatment to foreign currency deposit units vis-a-vis peso deposits in order to eliminate foreign exchange risks that could impose a heavy toll on monetary management (BUSINESS DAILY)
- The Department of Finance is considering imposing a road user's tax which will be used for road maintenance (BUSINESSWORLD)
